items: Convention: colon-delimited `object-type:id:field`
Redis does not enforce it; tooling and `SCAN` rely on it
`TYPE key` reports the stored type
Commands are type-checked before they run
Every command runs to completion, atomically
No locks or transactions needed for one command
One O(N) command over 1M elements blocks all clients
Latency is a shared resource, not a per-client budget

blocks.title: Consequence
blocks.text: Big-O is per command, but the stall is per server. A 40 ms `SMEMBERS` is 40 ms of silence for every other connection.

blocks.text: A job queue with no cap and no `BLMOVE`: unbounded growth on a producer spike, and silent job loss the moment a worker crashes mid-task.

caption.text: Most Redis outages are not Redis being slow — they are one O(N) command holding a single-threaded server hostage while 500 clients wait. This handbook walks all five core types: their internal encodings, the commands worth memorising, the Big-O of each, and the exact mistakes (KEYS *, SMEMBERS, HGETALL on a 100k-field bucket) that turn a cache into a stall. Ten pages, from the flat keyspace to SLOWLOG.
